topicName: Supply Chain Security and Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Supply Chain Security and Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) in CI/CD"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern software development relies heavily on open-source libraries, third-party packages, and automated deployment pipelines. While this accelerates delivery, it also introduces significant supply chain risks. Securing your CI/CD pipeline and generating a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) are critical practices to ensure software integrity and transparency."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Supply Chain Security in CI/CD"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A software supply chain encompasses every component, tool, and process used to build and deploy an application. Securing the CI/CD pipeline means protecting the build environment, verifying dependencies, and signing artifacts to prevent tampering at any stage of the lifecycle."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Dependency Confusion: Attackers publish malicious packages with the same names as internal dependencies."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Compromised Build Agents: Attackers inject malicious scripts into runner environments."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Unverified Artifacts: Deploying binaries without proving who built them and from what source."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"The Role of Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"An SBOM is a formal, structured list of components and supply chain relationships that make up a software artifact. Think of it as an ingredient list for your software. Generating an SBOM during the CI/CD process allows security teams to quickly identify vulnerable dependencies when new Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) are disclosed."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing SBOM Generation in GitHub Actions"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is an example of a GitHub Actions workflow that builds a container image, scans it for vulnerabilities, and generates an SBOM using Syft, a popular tool for generating software bills of materials."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"name: Secure CI/CD Pipeline
on: [push]
jobs:
  build-and-sbom:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Build Docker Image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          tags: myapp:latest
          load: true

      - name: Install Syft
        run: curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh -s -- -b /usr/local/bin

      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: syft myapp:latest -o spdx-json=sbom.json

      - name: Upload SBOM Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-sbom
          path: sbom.json"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Supply Chain Hardening"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pin Dependencies: Always use exact version hashes or specific tags rather than floating tags like latest."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Sign Artifacts: Use tools like Cosign to cryptographically sign container images and SBOMs."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enforce Least Privilege: Restrict permissions on CI/CD runner tokens and secrets."},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining robust CI/CD pipeline security controls with automated SBOM generation, organizations can significantly reduce their risk surface and achieve compliance with modern software security standards."}]
